I will start from what worked for me last year and only adjust where the numbers make sense. On 18.4 mu with only 2 people at home, I have to keep labor efficiency in mind, so I will not spread myself too thin with fussy management. I have well irrigation, so I can push yield a bit harder than dryland farmers around me, especially on wheat and maize. Cotton is still my main crop, but I will keep some wheat and maize because they spread risk and give me steadier cash flow across the year. Since fertilizer is expensive but yield loss is worse, I will not cut nitrogen too hard. I will keep phosphorus steady for root growth and early vigor, and I will hold enough potassium on cotton because cotton pulls hard on potash and I have seen weak boll set when K is short. On the better, flatter land with easier irrigation, I will put wheat and maize. On the fields where I can manage longer season picking and irrigation, I will keep cotton. I do not chase fancy changes just because someone says so, but if hybrid maize and improved wheat seed give stable performance, I will use them. Tillage-wise, I will keep rotary tillage where it saves time and moisture, and no-tillage for maize where I want to move fast after the previous crop. My target this year is steady output, controlled labor, and no obvious nutrient shortage at key growth stages.
